sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, written from memory BEFORE document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: Merck re-rated because the market decided Keytruda's 2028 cliff is solved (subQ Keytruda plus the acquired pipeline) and that the H1-2026 losses are one-off charges — so MRK reads as a de-risked compounder, not a patent-cliff name.

sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
Sources: `data/dossiers/MRK.md` (asof 2026-10-21) — annual, quarterly, balance-sheet and cash-flow tables. No primary filing is in-repo; load-bearing lines cite dossier lines.

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS gate — the card's question 1.** Revenue is FLAT, not falling: H1-26 $32.9bn (16.3 + 16.6) vs ~$31.3bn derived for H1-25 (FY25 65.0 less H2-25 17.3 + 16.4). So the ~-$15bn EBIT swing (H1-25 ~+11.4 to H1-26 -3.6) cannot be a gross-margin event — the charge sits *inside* operating income. Three dossier lines support a one-off:
1. FY2023 is the same shape and RESOLVED: EBIT $3.0bn, EPS $0.14, then EPS $6.74 on revenue growth of +6.8% — a 48x EPS recovery on 6.8% growth only happens if the depressed year was non-recurring.
2. FY2023 cash did not collapse: OCF $13.0bn against net income $0.4bn (CFO/NI 35.6x) — a non-cash charge depresses GAAP EBIT and leaves cash intact.
3. Accruals clean: FY25 (18.3-16.5)/127 = 1.4%. (Receivables/inventory data: unavailable.)

**Ruling: charge-driven (acquisition IPR&D / litigation), NOT operating deterioration** — optics-class. Honest limit: the dossier does NOT itemise the H1-26 charge, so this is shape-plus-precedent inference, not line-verified — the weakest joint. FY2026 is the crushed year; FY27-28 normalise to the FY2025 margin.

**Revenue (USD bn):** 65.0A (+1.2%) → 66.0E → 68.0E (+3.0%) → 69.5E. Load-bearing: (i) low-single-digit growth — FY25 +1.2%, quarterly revenue flat at $16.3-16.6bn; (ii) +3% FY27 from subQ Keytruda plus Winrevair/Ohtuvayre — analyst judgment, the widest error bar. Keytruda unit revenue is not itemised in-repo (cite-gap).

**Margins:** FY25A 34.0% → FY26E 10.6% (H1 -3.6 plus H2-26E ~+10.5) → FY27E 34.1% / FY28E 34.0%, flat — no expansion claimed. NI = 0.82 x EBIT. Diluted shares 2,514m falling ~1%/yr.

sections.heading: Valuation, the re-rate case and EV math
sections.markdown:
Market context: $145.27 (2026-10-23 close, `fund record`); mom12 +73.87%, mom6 +31.53%, mom1 -1.83%, off 52w high -6.60%, vol 35.8%, corr_bench 0.08, ADV $1.489bn; mcap $356.0bn (`the market-cap feed`). Reversal filter: mom1 -1.83% PASSES.

**Q2 — what re-rated, and does it survive the FY27 guide.** The +74% 12m move came on revenue growth of +1.2%; FY25 EPS $7.28 is only +8% over FY24's $6.74. It was a pure multiple re-rating, ~11x → ~20x trailing, on the market's decision that the 2028 US Keytruda cliff is solved (subQ Keytruda plus the acquired pipeline — Verona's Ohtuvayre is now in the dossier's brand list). The FY2027 guide is the one datapoint narrative cannot reverse: the dated review sits there.

**Q3 — Keytruda schedule / pipeline replacement NPV: NOT underwritten.** The dossier itemises neither Keytruda revenue nor LOE dates, so no replacement NPV is computed. This thesis does not claim to have solved the cliff; it claims the market has already paid for a solution. That is the ceiling on conviction.

**Method.** P/E on forward earnings (the card's engine), capped at the current multiple: base 18x FY2028E $7.92 = 143; bull 21x FY2028E bull $8.75 = 184; bear 14x FY2027E $7.68 = 108. FY25 FCF $12.4bn on a $356bn cap is a 3.5% FCF yield — no cash-flow support for 20x unless the cliff is covered.

**EV math (TARGET-FIRST, kill-second).** Target 184 / kill 108 / entry 135. up = +36.3%; down = -20.0%; ratio 1.81 vs momentum library 1.36 — no symmetry defect. p_up 0.50 — registry anchor, zero deviation. carry = 2.5 x 0.75 - 0.5 = 1.375; expected = 0.5(36.3) + 0.5(-20.0) + 1.375 = **+9.53% over 0.75y = +12.7%/yr vs the 11%/yr GLOBAL hurdle: CLEARS.** Kelly: own +112 vs library +61 (x10^4) — positive and above library; the gap is payoff and entry, not a shaded prior.

**WIN-STATE CHECK:** at p_up = 1.0, 36.3 + 2.5x0.75 - 0.5 = **+37.7%** over 0.75y vs the hurdle 11%/yr x 0.75y = 8.25% — clears by +29.4pp. NOT dead on arrival.

**Entry honesty:** at $145.27 the base case (143) sits 1.6% BELOW spot — the market already pays full value for the recovery. Entry 135 is 7.1% below spot and 5.9% below base fair value: a resting limit, not an endorsement of spot.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** the H1-2026 losses are one-off charges (correct) and that subQ Keytruda plus the acquired pipeline cover the 2028 cliff (the re-rate driver), so MRK is a de-risked defensive compounder worth ~20x.

**Why wrong:** the re-rate has already been paid. Normalising the charges gives FY2028E EPS ~$7.9, only ~+8% over FY2025 — the multiple doubled for earnings that barely move. The outcome from here is asymmetric against us: the multiple is the entire 12m return, and the multiple is what unwinds in the bear. Mechanically, FY2026 GAAP EPS ~$2.2 puts trailing P/E near 65x — a de-rating trigger for screens and style boxes before any FY2027 guide arrives.

**What proves us wrong:** the FY2027 guide showing revenue growth >=3% with EBIT ex-charges at/above the 2026 H2 run-rate and no margin give-back; subQ Keytruda conversion demonstrably revenue-accretive; a Keytruda LOE schedule pushed later than 2028.

**Edge taxonomy:** (a) analytical — the reported-vs-normalised decomposition locates *where* the mispricing sits, not that the stock is cheap: at base 143 the price already embeds the recovery, so the edge lives entirely in the entry price. No (b)/(c)/(d).

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, each citing a dossier line
sections.markdown:
1. FY2025 revenue grew only +1.2% ($64.2bn → $65.0bn); quarterly revenue is flat at $16.3-16.6bn — the top line does not support a doubled multiple (annual + quarterly tables).
2. FY2025 CFO/NI 0.90x (OCF $16.5bn vs NI $18.3bn) — income modestly ahead of cash, a mild accrual flag (derived ratios).
3. FY2025 net debt $34.7bn; net debt/EBITDA 1.23x, up from 0.93x — acquisitions funded on the balance sheet (balance-sheet table, derived ratios).
4. The H1-2026 -$15bn EBIT swing is un-itemised in-repo: the one-off claim is inference, not a filed line — if any part is operating, FY27-28 normalisation is too high (quarterly table).

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is 2027-08 and this position lost 30%. Most likely: the H1-2026 losses were not one-off — part of the charge recurred in H2-2026 and the FY2027 guide showed EBIT ex-charges at/below the 2026 H2 run-rate — so the market reverted to pricing Merck as a cliff-facing pharma and the multiple unwound from ~20x to ~14x, my 108 kill, with no revenue offset because the top line never grew. Second: Keytruda LOE guidance moved earlier and subQ conversion proved volume-neutral. Lesson either way: I bought a multiple that had already doubled on flat earnings, and I could not verify the charge decomposition from any in-repo filing.
